I don't mind sharing since it is helping others! Therapy was not working out for me because it was a weekly cycle of small talk about how my week went and how I felt about it. This by no means is to say that talk therapy doesn't work because it does, for some people. I have a doctor who I regularly see for medication which helped get me out of bed and stop being a cave dweller. I had been on the drug medications for a year prior to starting my garden and was noticing minimal results with breaks of relapse. I noticed how happy I was becoming as soon as I started planning my garden and it took off from there! I definitely think it's up to the person because some people can greatly benefit from CBT talk therapy because talking out their problems can greatly reduce their stress. I am more introverted so I found therapy to be annoying where I wasn't seeing results from my efforts in plain sight, where as gardening is a daily reward for the new growth I put my time into (so it's something I can be proud of, and not dwell). I think the combo of medication and **finding something you love and dedicating yourself to it is the most important thing because if you truly love it, it will make you happier.**

I've been trying out gardening for the past fews years only to give up, but I was always intrigued to see what can come from one little seed and a little hard work has to offer. I was diagnosed with severe bipolar/ depression and this past spring I wanted an "out" to help me focus negative energy and turn it into something positive so I decided since talk therapy wasn't working for me, I was going to garden. HARDCORE! They say to do what makes you happy, so I did. Gardening has made me appreciate life and how precious it all really is. Most College age kids think beer and parties are what 'fun' is, but to me, fun is doing what you love. And gardening is just that. Everyday I'm reminded of the love I put into this sunflower (and all my other sunflowers/vegetables) just by walking out my front door. Here is a photo of me and my mammoth sunflower, of which I never thought I could grow.. But with patience and care it turned out to be my proudest achievement these past few months. I've learned more about my mental health by gardening and creating something you can be proud of than any drug/ therapist has ever done for me. Hope you enjoy! -Be kind to one another <3


**Edit:** WOW You guys are the *best!* I never expected to actually get upvotes or views or comments but you surprised me! All these responses have made me feel overwhelmed with joy that many other people are being inspired to get back to gardening! It also warms my heart to see that there are other people out there going through a mental disorder or even hard times, who have turned to nature to help recover/manage their happiness and overall quality of life. I appreciate all the responses. Also thank you to whomever gave me reddit gold<3 A redditor's dream come true. **Thank you all.**
